metformin.missed_dose_rule: Take as soon as remembered with a meal. If close to the next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume normal schedule. DO NOT take extra medicine to make up for a missed dose. Note: In monotherapy, metformin carries low intrinsic hypoglycaemia risk, but arbitrary dose doubling increases acute gastrointestinal toxicity and adverse metabolic effects.
metformin.red_flags: Lactic acidosis symptoms: severe somnolence, unexplained muscle pain, severe abdominal discomfort, hypothermia, or rapid deep breathing.

propranolol.administration_rule: Swallow sustained-release (LA) formulations whole. Do not crush, chew, or divide. Take consistently either with food or on an empty stomach to avoid bioavailability swings.
propranolol.red_flags: Severe bradycardia, worsening breathlessness, wheezing, or profound postural lightheadedness.

lorazepam.administration_rule: Mouth dissolving (MD) tablets dissolve rapidly on the tongue without additional water. Strictly avoid alcohol and concurrent central nervous system depressants without medical authorization.
lorazepam.red_flags: Extreme daytime somnolence, slowed shallow breathing, unsteadiness causing severe fall risk, or paradoxical agitation.

methotrexate.dosage_frequency_safety: WEEKLY ONLY for rheumatoid arthritis/psoriasis. NEVER DAILY. Accidental daily dosing causes fatal bone marrow suppression and gastrointestinal toxicity.
methotrexate.red_flags: Oral mucosal ulceration, unexplained bleeding, high fever, or persistent sore throat indicating acute neutropenia.

critical_interactions: Nitrates (e.g., Nitroglycerin, Isosorbide Dinitrate/Mononitrate, Nicorandil): Absolute contraindication due to life-threatening synergistic hypotension.
sildenafil.red_flags: Severe unresolving chest pressure, profound hypotension, sudden visual disturbance, or painful priapism exceeding 4 hours.

paracetamol.maximum_dose_rule: Maximum 4000 mg (4 g) per 24 hours in adults with normal hepatic function. Check all concurrent over-the-counter cold and cough preparations to avoid inadvertent duplicate paracetamol poisoning.
paracetamol.red_flags: Right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or jaundice indicating acute hepatotoxicity from overdose.
